asks: Why are stop, restore and drop destructive?
answer: Stop, restore and drop are destructive for what they end: the programs running in the computer and what they hold in memory, which a checkpoint of the disk does not keep. A restore first saves where you were (`restore-saves-first`), so it erases nothing on the disk. If checkpoints come to keep memory, as forks of running Linux computers would need, whether these three stay destructive is asked again.
